contexts.text: A pictured image of the man (in each idea of his thought).
The ideas themselves appear (there) like pictured images.
To paint with vermilion () = to falsify spiritual truths.
Beauty from the truth of faith only is like the beauty of a painted or sculptured face...

Like flowers painted upon a tablet, as compared with those born in a garden... The flowers painted on a tablet are beautiful in the external form only; and as to the internal one are nothing but dirt and a mass of earthy particles lying strewed about... So is it with the good which is from man, as compared with that which is from the Lord. AC 8801:end.
Like a painting in the likeness of a man, in which inwardly there is nothing but dirt, as compared with the form of the man himself, in which inwardly there is life.
Men painted on the wall () = the appearances of truth in externals: in like manner images painted with vermilion.
This truth (without good) may be likened to paintings of flowers, of a tree, of an animal, inwardly in which there is only dirt...
The Angels in churches, whether sculptured or painted, are always presented as men.
No painter with all his art could give such light to the colours...
When God is presented in pictures as a Man.
Paint, etc. () = the spiritual things of worship. AR 777:2, Illustrated.
No painter could present her beauty in its form; for there is no such lustre in his colour; nor is such beauty expressible in his art.
Painted like rainbow stones.
Like a picture on a wall seen at night...
Should see on a tablet (the three gods) painted...
Therefore painters set an ugly face beside a handsome one. TCR 465. TCR 763.
If this faith were exhibited in its enormity in a picture...
Faith separated is like a painting in colours partaking of black on a black stone; but faith conjoined is like a painting in beautiful colours on a transparent crystal.
The (mere) name of a Christian... is like a blackened painting.
Images, paintings, and innumerable other things, which in outermosts appear beautiful, and are esteemed as of great price, are yet so disposed within that they are like dirt and mud... SE 2558.
These things have been shown me, but I cannot describe the forms and pictures... They can indeed be pictured, but not described to the apprehension.
As I have somewhere seen in pictures.
Therefore they tolerate in their temples neither statues, images, nor pictures...
As when one sees in a picture everything represented simultaneously.
Not as if they were painted, but seen...
Like pictured things which appear optically.
Recognized him from his picture in the world.

When she saw men painted upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans painted with vermilion () = phantasies from the fallacies of the senses, which are of the sensuous man; and the derivative argumentations, whence are falsifications.
(Such works) are like paintings made from stercoraceous dirt coloured over...
The Temple, in which... the paintings, etc., were representative.
Painted with vermilion = these things appearing exteriorly like truths... The painted wall = the appearance of the doctrinal things in externals.
Cannot be imitated by any picture in the world.
The ancients, when they represented God in their paintings, pictured Him as a Man...
